document.title: Ask the agent why: intent questions on groups
document.summary: Each group can hold at most 2 `questions` about intent. The group brief lists them under the attention with an Ask agent button, agent-md and What changed show them, refresh counts them, and the skill and eval learn the rule.
document.why: [#162](source:s1) asks for questions about intent on each group, because the agent that wrote the change is often in the same session and asking it why is cheap.

sources.title: Intent questions on groups
sources.gist: Group questions (at most 2) about intent, with an Ask agent button, across every layer.

sources.label: PR #169
sources.title: Ask the agent why: intent questions on groups

sources.label: PR #168
sources.title: Replace group lookFor with one typed attention per group
sources.gist: Lower layer of the stack: group attention, which questions sit under.

lookFor: [#162](source:s1) says `refresh` re-checks the questions of the groups its report names. At head `formatRefresh` only appends `N questions to re-check` to each named group line; the skill's Refresh step 4 does the re-check. [PR #169](source:s2) gives this split as a decision.

groups.title: Questions field, at most 2
groups.why: [#162](source:s1) asks for group `questions?: string[]`, at most 2. The type and `validate` both carry the limit.
groups.summary: `questionsSchema` in `review.ts` is a union of `[]`, `[q]`, and `[q, q]`, so `Questions` is a tuple type and a third question fails parse; `source.ts` checks citations in questions, and `parse.test.ts` pins the limit.

attention.note: The tuple union makes the JSON schema an `anyOf` of three tuples instead of `maxItems: 2`. Agents read that JSON schema in `references/review.schema.json`. Decide whether the typed limit is worth the noisier schema.

groups.title: Questions in agent markdown and the prompt
groups.why: [#162](source:s1) asks for a `Questions:` block in `agent-md.ts` and a button prompt that reuses `agentClipboardPrompt`.
groups.summary: `live.ts` puts `questions` on each `ApiReview` group, `questionsBlock` prints them in the group and overview markdown, and `agentClipboardPrompt(url, question?)` appends one question after the URL.

groups.title: Questions under the attention
groups.why: [#162](source:s1) asks for the questions under the group attention, each with an Ask agent button.
groups.summary: `GroupBrief` renders `QuestionList` after `AttentionAlert`, and each row uses `CopyPrompt` with the new `question` scope, a ghost Ask agent button that copies `askAgentPrompt({ group }, question)`.

groups.title: Questions on What changed
groups.why: [#162](source:s1) asks What changed to list questions that were added or removed.
groups.summary: `changesPayload` sets `questions` with `listChange` for kept and new groups, `hasChange` counts it, and `Changes.tsx` shows it as a Questions list beside the attention.

groups.title: Refresh counts questions to re-check
groups.why: [#162](source:s1) asks refresh to re-check the questions of the groups its report names.
groups.summary: `formatRefresh` appends `N questions to re-check` to each named group that is not `now empty`, and the tests pin it for a unit document and the mixed fixture.

groups.title: Skill rule, example, and glossary
groups.why: [#162](source:s1) proposes the rule: ask why when the code and the sources leave the reason open, and put a source's answer in `why`.
groups.summary: A new Questions section in `skills-next/comprehende/SKILL.md` states the rule, steps 4 and Refresh 4 use it, `example.md` adds the issue's two questions, and the glossary defines Questions; the `.agents/` copies are the `sync:skill` output of the same text.

groups.title: Eval: question Must nots and grader input
groups.why: [#162](source:s1) asks for a Must-not entry, a question that a source answers.
groups.summary: Ten `expected.md` files gain a case-specific Must not for a question a source answers and two gain a Good entry for an open intent, while `packet.ts`, `checks.ts`, and `graders.ts` pass questions to the grader and the prose lint.

attention.note: `graders.ts` now lets a group question state a Must or Good fact. A question like "Why does X drop `Max-Age`?" also says that X drops it, so Must scores can rise a little against runs before this change.

groups.title: Generated JSON schema copies
groups.why: `pnpm generate:schema` and `pnpm sync:skill` write these from `review.ts`.
groups.summary: The three `review.schema.json` files are the same generated output with the new `questions` entry, so the reader can skip them after the schema group.

commits.subject: Add group intent questions with an Ask agent button
commits.author: Máté Molnár
commits.body:
Groups carry at most 2 questions about intent, typed as a tuple so the
type and validate both hold the limit. The group brief lists them under
the attention, each with an Ask agent button that copies the group
prompt plus the question. agent-md gets a Questions block, What changed
lists added and removed questions, and the refresh report counts the
questions of each named group to re-check. The skill, example,
glossary, eval criteria, and case expectations follow.

Closes #162

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
